question: How do you prevent duplicate database or API queries when both generateMetadata and the default Page component need the same product record?
options: Store the product record on the global window object inside generateMetadata
Wrap the shared data-fetching function in React.cache (or use fetch) so calls with identical arguments are memoized within the same request pass
Pass the return value of generateMetadata as a prop into the Page component
Disable generateMetadata on dynamic routes and inject meta tags inside useEffect
explanation: React.cache and Next.js fetch memoization deduplicate identical requests across generateMetadata, layouts, and page components during a single server render pass.

question: What security and cost risk does setting images.qualities: [75] in next.config.ts mitigate?
options: It prevents users from right-clicking and saving images in the browser
It stops attackers from requesting arbitrary quality query parameters (such as q=1 through q=100) to trigger excessive image re-encoding and cache storage exhaustion
It forces all SVG icons to execute inline JavaScript inside the browser
It disables HTTPS certificate verification when fetching remote images
explanation: Restricting images.qualities to an explicit allowlist like [75] blocks malicious requests that vary the quality parameter to multiply image transformations and CDN cache entries.

question: How does next/font eliminate Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) caused by web fonts?
options: It hides the entire document body for five seconds until all third-party CDN scripts finish loading
It downloads font files at build time to self-host them with your static assets and applies size-adjusted CSS fallback metrics so text dimensions remain stable
It converts every paragraph of text into a raster PNG image on the server
It disables custom fonts on mobile viewports automatically
explanation: next/font self-hosts font files at build time—removing runtime requests to external font origins—and generates matching fallback font metrics to prevent layout shifts.

question: What is the rendering trade-off of generating a per-request Content Security Policy (CSP) nonce in proxy.ts and reading it via await headers() in a layout?
options: The route must render dynamically per request because a cryptographic nonce cannot be reused across cached static HTML responses
Client Components inside the route can no longer attach onClick event handlers
All next/image components on the page revert to unstyled anchor tags
The browser disables HTTP/2 multiplexing for the entire domain
explanation: A CSP nonce must be freshly generated for every response; reading it from request headers opts the route into dynamic rendering so each visitor receives a unique nonce.
